title: Rav Abbahu (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was one of the heads of the kallah of Rafram (who headed the academy in Pumbedita from the year 744 until 754, Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 3), according to the testimony of his son Rav Shmuel, Chullin 49a; and Rav Shmuel his son was one of the Savoraim. In Bava Kamma 117a, Rav Abbahu raised an objection to Rav Ashi; Seder HaDorot wrote that this is the earlier Rav Ashi; Hyman rejects this, for the Gemara there makes clear that it is Rav Ashi, Ravina’s colleague. In Yevamot 26a, according to the reading of Or Zarua HaGadol, Rabbi Abbahu said to Rav Ashi, “But it was taught: Even if they were divorced”; Hyman’s received reading is Rav Hillel. Hyman suggests that possibly the phrase always found, “Rabbi Abbahu scoffed at it,” refers to this Rabbi Abbahu.

notes.text: מגדף בה is scoffing at a teaching, not blasphemy. The years744–754 remain without an invented era. Hyman’s Rav Abbahu versus saved Davidson Rabbi Abbahu in Chullin49a/Bava Kamma117a is a named-witness title difference; Yevamot26a has Rav Hillel. The Savora and Rav Ashi identifications remain Hyman’s argument.

The consulted Chullin 49a and Bava Kamma 117a use Rabbi Abbahu, while Hyman supplies Rav Abbahu. Yevamot 26a has Rav Hillel speaking to Rav Ashi. Hyman’s Or Zarua alternative, Savora classification, Rav Ashi identification and possible scoffing-formula identification remain attributed; years 744–754 receive no invented era.
